questions.answer: No; a person can accept practical support while maintaining privacy.

questions.prompt: Why clarify purpose before asking questions?
questions.answer: It helps limit unnecessary information collection.

questions.prompt: Can a peer always promise absolute confidentiality?
questions.answer: No; actual duties and safety concerns may impose limits.

questions.prompt: What takes priority when immediate danger arises?
questions.feedback: Do not delay for ordinary discussion.

scoring.knowledge: 1 point per correct answer; formative only.
scoring.practice: Demonstrates permission-based communication, privacy and refusal boundaries, and appropriate safety exceptions.
scoring.transfer: Write a fictional exchange in which someone declines to discuss a loss. Include a practical offer, an alternative contact if wanted and a privacy boundary. Explain how the response changes if immediate danger is reported.
scoring.pass: All mapped criteria require Level 2 evidence; no averaging away omissions or safety-critical criteria. No automatic competency award.
